_meta.title: Orbit Accord negotiation process: candidate rules
_meta.status: proposed fictional mechanics; grounded in precedent, not measured probabilities
_meta.warning: All numbers below are invented game weights for tuning. They are not acceptance probabilities and must not be displayed as such.

current_mechanics.name: single acceptance roll
current_mechanics.problem: one number mixes interest, authority, reciprocity and luck

current_mechanics.name: binary coalition
current_mechanics.problem: a country joins all six conditions at once, instantly

current_mechanics.name: free promise
current_mechanics.problem: promises are labels; never stored, delivered or checked

current_mechanics.name: monthly amnesia
current_mechanics.problem: refusals leave no reason and no consequence

rules.name: Two-step consent
rules.objective: keep the visible promise inside the official's actual authority
rules.authority_instrument: ministerial signature, cabinet/legislative referral, or regulator procedure
rules.trigger: player makes an offer in a meeting
rules.conditions: decision class from decision_function; refers requires named approver and date
rules.plausible_response: I can sign the incident rule today; testing needs my minister.
rules.substitute: narrower offer that fits the envoy's authority
rules.evidence_limit: neither source is an AI-safety accord among middle powers; they show sequence, not likelihood
rules.game_mapping: add state 'refers', next_date, and an authority label on the meeting card

rules.name: Scope-limited participation
rules.objective: avoid rejecting a package because of one unacceptable element
rules.authority_instrument: schedule of commitments rather than one yes/no
rules.conditions: partner selects a subset of conditions; accord strength per condition counts only members of that condition
rules.plausible_response: We will join the alarm and the off-switch. Not chip tracking.
rules.substitute: full package, which the partner may refuse
rules.evidence_limit: both are trade instruments; scope breadth is a design choice

rules.name: Approval clock
rules.objective: make domestic authority the binding constraint
rules.authority_instrument: legislative window, regulator rulemaking, joint decision
rules.conditions: decision at next_date; fails if window closed or reliability fell
rules.plausible_response: My government will deliberate. Its answer comes by official letter.
rules.substitute: ask a partner with ministerial authority, or narrow the ask
rules.evidence_limit: shows approval bodies exist and timelines change; not how a cabinet would treat a fictional accord
rules.game_mapping: reuse the existing letter screen; add the deciding body and the date

rules.name: Phased delivery with verification gates
rules.objective: tie each benefit to an observed step
rules.authority_instrument: staged annex with dates and a named verifying body
rules.conditions: 2-3 stages; benefit releases only after matching stage is verified
rules.plausible_response: Relief only after the inspector confirms the steps.
rules.substitute: upfront release, usually refused after any breach
rules.evidence_limit: JCPOA has a dedicated inspectorate; an AI accord has none, so the verifier must be labelled fictional
rules.game_mapping: add stages[] with due month and status to each signed condition

rules.name: Reciprocity ledger
rules.objective: make exchange legible and reversible without drama
rules.authority_instrument: ledger with one line per commitment and per benefit
rules.trigger: any offer including a token or market access
rules.conditions: benefit marked held, released or withheld, with a date
rules.plausible_response: The payment is approved but not disbursed until the report arrives.
rules.substitute: unconditional gift, which raises expectations of more gifts
rules.evidence_limit: game benefit is a token, not money; sources show linkage between reporting and standing
rules.game_mapping: add benefit_status and benefit_date; show in HUD

rules.name: Issue-specific reliability record
rules.objective: let past behaviour change future terms visibly
rules.authority_instrument: per-condition record kept by the accord (fictional secretariat)
rules.trigger: every verified, late or missed stage
rules.conditions: counts per condition, shown before an offer
rules.plausible_response: Last time your report was two months late. We want a monitor this time.
rules.substitute: new partner with no record; narrower ask
rules.evidence_limit: membership organisations with boards; the record is a simplification, not a trust score

rules.name: Record triggers safeguards, not just refusal
rules.objective: continue cooperating while managing observed risk
rules.authority_instrument: third-party check, escrow/staged release, named monitor
rules.conditions: safeguard added to the deal card as a visible cost
rules.plausible_response: We will join, but the benefit stays in escrow until the first inspection.
rules.substitute: decline, or accept lower scope with no benefit
rules.evidence_limit: snapback is unique and contested; it overstates how fast an AI accord could re-impose anything
rules.game_mapping: modify the deal card, never the hidden roll

rules.name: Windows create authority, not consent (optional)
rules.objective: make the calendar matter without making it magic
rules.trigger: data/windows.json date reached for that country and condition
rules.conditions: open window lets refers decide this month; missed window delays 6-12 months
rules.plausible_response: The bill is tabled; after that we wait for the next session.
rules.evidence_limit: window dates are research inputs owned by other notes and are not verified here
rules.game_mapping: windows.json already exists; only the effect changes

player_facing_strings.signs: Can sign today. Their minister has the authority.
player_facing_strings.refers: Signed, not yet in force. Their parliament votes by {month}.
player_facing_strings.conditions: Will sign if {fix}. Nothing else needs to change.
player_facing_strings.declines_fixable: No while the ask includes {condition}. Bring {narrower} alone.
player_facing_strings.delivering: In force, delivering: {k} of {n} stages done. Next: {stage}, {month}.
player_facing_strings.late: Late. {partner} has not received the {stage}. Reliability on {condition} down.

acceptance_checks.test: meeting card shows interest, authority, scope, dated next step
no percentage shown as acceptance chance
changing one visible input changes outcome in predicted direction
partner joining two conditions appears only for those two
every signed condition shows k/n stages and a date
missed delivery produces a safeguard line naming it, on that condition only
pausing a condition removes its contribution, shows reason, is reversible
five cold players can say who decides and what happens next

limitations: precedents are analogues from trade, arms control, climate and extractives, not AI-safety accords
eight-month campaign compresses approval that takes months to years in reality
Gulf states and Australia+Canada are grouped; collective authority is a placeholder
no real AI verification institution exists; the verifier in R4 is fictional and must be labelled so
data/windows.json dates are inputs owned by other research notes and are not verified here
no claim about the intentions of any real government
